title: Velcro hook-and-loop fastener
summary: The original hook-and-loop fastener patent — de Mestral's 'velvet type fabric' inspired by burrs catching on wool. Long expired and in the public domain; the mechanism underpins reusable fastening in textiles, medical wraps, and industrial assembly.
authors: George de Mestral

title: LEGO interlocking toy building brick
summary: The clutch-power stud-and-tube coupling that made the modern LEGO brick. The utility patent expired decades ago, placing the interlocking-brick geometry in the public domain for construction toys and modular tooling.
authors: Godtfred Kirk Christiansen

title: PageRank — node ranking in a linked database
summary: The PageRank algorithm that launched Google — ranks nodes in a linked graph by the weighted importance of inbound links. The patent has expired, so the method is free to build on for search, citation analysis, and network science.
authors: Lawrence Page

title: PCR — nucleic acid amplification process
summary: The polymerase chain reaction — exponential amplification of DNA sequences that transformed molecular biology and diagnostics. The foundational Cetus/Mullis patents have expired and PCR is now universally practiced.
authors: Kary B. Mullis et al.

title: Cohen–Boyer recombinant DNA method
summary: The Cohen–Boyer process for producing biologically functional molecular chimeras — the birth of recombinant DNA and the biotech industry. Now expired and in the public domain.
authors: Stanley N. Cohen, Herbert W. Boyer

title: Fused deposition modeling (FDM) 3D printing
summary: The original fused deposition modeling patent — building 3D objects by extruding material layer by layer. Its expiry in the 2000s triggered the desktop 3D-printing boom (RepRap, MakerBot, and beyond).
authors: S. Scott Crump

title: Nylon synthetic polyamide fiber
summary: Carothers' synthetic-fiber patent — the invention of nylon, the first fully synthetic polyamide fiber. Public domain; the condensation-polymer chemistry underlies modern textiles and engineering plastics.
authors: Wallace H. Carothers
organization: E.I. du Pont de Nemours & Co.

title: Linear condensation polymers (nylon chemistry)
summary: The companion Carothers patent covering linear condensation polymers — the polymerization route to nylon and polyester. Long expired; a cornerstone of synthetic-polymer manufacturing.
authors: Wallace H. Carothers
organization: E.I. du Pont de Nemours & Co.

title: Concentrator photovoltaic solar cell
summary: An early concentrator-photovoltaic design pairing solar cells with light concentrators to raise output per cell. Expired and open to build on for low-cost solar hardware.

title: Apple II microcomputer color video display
summary: Wozniak's patent for the Apple II's efficient color video display generation from a microcomputer. Now public domain — a piece of foundational personal-computing hardware.
authors: Stephen Wozniak

title: Xerography — electrophotography
summary: Carlson's electrophotography patent — the dry-toner imaging process that became xerographic copying and laser printing. Expired; the electrostatic-imaging principles remain widely used.
authors: Chester F. Carlson

title: Semisynthetic preparation of Taxol (paclitaxel)
summary: A practical semisynthetic route to the anticancer drug Taxol (paclitaxel) via an oxazinone intermediate. The process patent has expired, opening the chemistry for generic manufacture.
authors: Robert A. Holton

title: Magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) power generation
summary: Generating electricity directly from an ionized high-pressure gas stream — magnetohydrodynamic power conversion with no moving parts. Expired; of renewed interest for high-efficiency topping cycles.

title: Lightweight truss-core structural panel
summary: Boeing's truss-core sandwich panel — a lightweight, stiff structural panel geometry for aerospace and transport. Expired and open for structural-materials work.

title: Bosch gasoline fuel-injection arrangement
summary: An early Bosch fuel-injection arrangement for internal-combustion engines — a precursor to modern electronic fuel injection. Public domain.

title: Electric drink mixer (blender precursor)
summary: One of the earliest electric drink-mixer patents — the motor-driven mixing appliance that evolved into the kitchen blender. Firmly in the public domain.

title: Comb-over method for concealing baldness
summary: The famously improbable 'method of concealing partial baldness' (the comb-over) — an issued, now-expired US utility patent. Included as a light-hearted, genuinely public-domain curiosity.
authors: Frank J. Smith, Donald J. Smith

title: RSA public-key cryptography
summary: The RSA cryptosystem — public-key encryption and digital signatures based on the difficulty of factoring large numbers. MIT's patent expired in 2000 and RSA is now unencumbered and ubiquitous.
authors: Rivest, Shamir, Adleman

title: Wright brothers' flying machine
summary: The Wright brothers' foundational aircraft patent, covering wing-warping roll control for a powered flying machine. Firmly in the public domain — the origin of controlled powered flight.
authors: Orville & Wilbur Wright

title: Edison incandescent electric lamp
summary: Edison's incandescent electric lamp — a high-resistance carbon filament in an evacuated glass bulb. One of the most consequential patents in history, long in the public domain.
authors: Thomas A. Edison

title: Bell's telephone (improvement in telegraphy)
summary: Alexander Graham Bell's telephone patent — transmitting speech electrically over a wire. Perhaps the most valuable patent ever granted; now public domain.
authors: Alexander Graham Bell

title: Barcode — classifying apparatus and method
summary: The original barcode patent — optically machine-readable classifying symbols (the 'bull's-eye' code) that evolved into the UPC. Expired and in the public domain.
authors: N. J. Woodland, B. Silver

title: Noyce monolithic integrated circuit
summary: Noyce's monolithic integrated-circuit patent — interconnected components on a single silicon chip, the basis of all modern microelectronics. Long expired.
authors: Robert N. Noyce

title: Bell Labs transistor (three-electrode element)
summary: The point-contact transistor patent from Bell Labs — the three-electrode semiconductor amplifying device that launched the electronics age. Public domain.
authors: Bardeen, Brattain, Shockley

title: Maser / laser communications system
summary: The Townes–Schawlow maser/laser patent — stimulated-emission amplification of coherent radiation. Foundational to lasers across manufacturing, medicine, and communications; now expired.
authors: Charles H. Townes, Arthur L. Schawlow

title: Ballpoint pen writing instrument
summary: The Bíró ballpoint-pen patent — a rotating ball delivering quick-drying ink. A ubiquitous everyday product, long in the public domain.
authors: László Bíró

title: MapReduce — efficient large-scale data processing
summary: The MapReduce programming model for processing massive datasets across clusters. Google placed this patent under its Open Patent Non-Assertion Pledge, so it can be freely used in open-source software (it directly inspired Apache Hadoop).
authors: Jeffrey Dean, Sanjay Ghemawat

title: Distributed and parallel large-scale data processing
summary: A companion MapReduce patent covering large-scale data processing in a distributed, parallel environment. Pledged royalty-free under Google's OPN Pledge for use in open-source projects.
authors: Jeffrey Dean, Sanjay Ghemawat

title: Plus Codes — compact codes for geographic locations
summary: The 'plus codes' open-location scheme that encodes any place on Earth into a short alphanumeric code. Covered by Google's OPN Pledge, enabling open addressing systems.

title: Server-side suggestion of browser preload operations
summary: A web-performance technique where the server suggests resources for the browser to preload. Part of Google's OPN-pledged patents, free to use in open-source browsers and servers.

title: Predicting user navigation events with directed graphs
summary: Predicting a user's next navigation using a directed graph of prior events to prefetch content. Pledged royalty-free under Google's Open Patent Non-Assertion Pledge.

title: Sandia open-source face covering and face-shield designs
summary: Open, freely licensed face-covering and face-shield designs released by Sandia National Laboratories under the Open COVID Pledge for pandemic response and beyond.

title: NASA JPL 3D-printed respirator design
summary: NASA JPL's 3D-printable respirator design, pledged for free use under the Open COVID Pledge. A ready reference for open medical-hardware manufacture.

title: Intel touchless authentication technology
summary: Intel's touchless password/authentication approach, made available royalty-free through the Open COVID Pledge to reduce shared-surface contact.

title: HPE Wi-Fi–enabled pop-up clinic and hospital design
summary: HPE's networked pop-up clinic/hospital design pledged under Open COVID for rapid deployment of connected temporary care facilities.

title: Fujitsu computational drug-discovery technique
summary: Fujitsu's software techniques to aid drug discovery, made freely available under the Open COVID Pledge to accelerate therapeutic research.

title: Aspirin — genericized trademark, now free to use
summary: Once Bayer's trademark, 'aspirin' was ruled generic in the United States (Bayer Co. v. United Drug Co., 1921) and is now a free common name for acetylsalicylic acid.

title: Cellophane — genericized trademark, now free to use
summary: DuPont's 'cellophane' became generic in the US (DuPont Cellophane Co. v. Waxed Products, 1936); the term now freely denotes transparent regenerated-cellulose film.

title: Escalator — genericized trademark, now free to use
summary: Otis lost the 'escalator' trademark to genericide in 1950; the word is now the ordinary term for a moving staircase.

title: Thermos — genericized trademark, now free to use
summary: A US court ruled 'thermos' generic in 1963 (King-Seeley Thermos Co. v. Aladdin); it now freely means a vacuum-insulated container.

title: Zipper — genericized trademark, now free to use
summary: Originally B.F. Goodrich's trademark for its galoshes' slide fastener, 'zipper' became the generic name for the interlocking fastener.

title: Trampoline — genericized trademark, now free to use
summary: Coined and trademarked by George Nissen, 'trampoline' passed into generic use for the rebound apparatus.

title: Dry Ice — genericized trademark, now free to use
summary: Trademarked in 1925, 'dry ice' became the generic name for solid carbon dioxide used in cooling and cleaning.

title: Kerosene — genericized trademark, now free to use
summary: Gesner's 1854 trademark 'kerosene' became the generic term for the refined petroleum lamp/heating fuel.

title: Linoleum — genericized trademark, now free to use
summary: Widely cited as the first trademark to become generic (UK, 1878) — 'linoleum' now freely denotes the linseed-oil-based floor covering.

title: Laundromat — genericized trademark, now free to use
summary: Westinghouse's 'Laundromat' became the generic US term for a self-service coin-operated laundry.

title: Videotape — genericized trademark, now free to use
summary: Ampex's 'videotape' passed into generic use for magnetic tape used to record video.

title: Yo-yo — genericized trademark, now free to use
summary: Duncan's 'Yo-Yo' trademark was ruled generic (1965) after the term became the common name for the spinning string toy.

title: Mimeograph — genericized trademark, now free to use
summary: A.B. Dick's 'Mimeograph' became the generic name for the stencil-based duplicating machine widely used before photocopiers.

title: Teleprompter — genericized trademark, now free to use
summary: The 'TelePrompTer' trademark genericized into 'teleprompter', the ordinary word for a scrolling speech-display device.

title: Touch-tone — genericized trademark, now free to use
summary: AT&T's 'Touch-Tone' mark for DTMF dialing passed into generic use for tone-based telephone dialing.

title: Dumpster — genericized trademark, now free to use
summary: From Dempster Brothers' 'Dumpster' (Dempster-Dumpster system); the trademark was cancelled and the word is now generic for a large mobile waste container.

title: Super Glue — genericized trademark, now free to use
summary: 'Super Glue' became a generic term for fast-setting cyanoacrylate adhesive after widespread descriptive use.

title: Hovercraft — genericized trademark, now free to use
summary: Saunders-Roe's 'hovercraft' became the generic name for the air-cushion vehicle.

title: Lanolin — genericized trademark, now free to use
summary: 'Lanolin' passed into generic use as the common name for purified wool wax used in cosmetics and pharmaceuticals.

title: Quonset hut — genericized trademark, now free to use
summary: 'Quonset', from Great Lakes Steel's prefabricated arched building, became the generic term for the lightweight semicylindrical structure.
